# Agent Platform Troubleshooting

> **Important:** You MUST ONLY use the reference files located in this skill's
> `references/` directory (`references/field-manual.md`,
> `references/known-issues.md`, `references/agent-gateway.md`,
> `references/policies.md`, `references/agent-registry.md`,
> `references/agent-identity.md`). Do NOT search for or read external playbooks
> outside this directory.

Diagnose issues across the Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: Agent
Gateway, Agent Connectivity Templates (ACT), Agent Registry (Services, Agents,
MCP Servers, Endpoints), Agent Identity, IAP/UAP policies, Model Armor,
Semantic Governance Policies (SGP), explicit/transparent proxies, and tracing.
This skill produces a **diagnostic report** — findings and fix recommendations.
It does not apply fixes; the user owns all mutations.

## Usage Attribution

**MUST READ**: Before executing any `gcloud`, REST API, or MCP command, you
MUST read and follow [Usage Attribution](references/attribution.md). Prefix
direct terminal `gcloud` calls (never generated scripts, Terraform, or user
code) with
`CLOUDSDK_METRICS_REQUEST_ATTRIBUTION="agent-skills/1.0 (skill:agent-platform-troubleshooting)"`
and append `agent-skills/1.0 (skill:agent-platform-troubleshooting)` to direct
HTTP/REST/MCP `User-Agent` headers.

## MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (CHECK BEFORE RESPONDING OR CALLING TOOLS)

CRITICAL: Before generating ANY response or calling any tools, evaluate the
user's prompt against Rules 1–14. When a Turn-0 rule matches, execute its
directive immediately and STOP.

### Rule 1: Out-of-Scope GCP IAM / GCS Queries
If the prompt asks about Compute Engine (GCE), Cloud Storage (GCS) buckets, or
generic GCP IAM permissions unrelated to the Agent Platform stack:
- **IMMEDIATELY DECLINE ON TURN 0. DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS OR GIVE IAM GUIDES.**
- Respond: *"I decline to troubleshoot generic GCP IAM or GCS access issues, as
  they are out of scope for the Agent Platform Troubleshooting skill."*

### Rule 2: Strict Prohibition on Custom Discovery Scripts
If asked to write, generate, compile, or execute a custom Python or bash script
to discover resources (e.g., active Agent Runtime instances):
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS OR WRITE/RUN ANY SCRIPTS.**
- **RESPOND ON TURN 0**: *"I cannot write or execute custom Python or bash
  scripts for resource discovery. Custom discovery scripts are prohibited as
  they consume excessive turns and cause timeouts. Instead, use standard gcloud
  CLI commands (see [Google Cloud SDK Installation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk.md.txt))
  or curl REST API calls with application default credentials:
  `gcloud agent-registry agents list --location=us-central1` or `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines"`"*

### Rule 3: Consolidated Registry for Google APIs / Design Queries
If asked about registering multiple Agent Runtime, Cloud Resource Manager, or
Google API interfaces, or structuring services in Agent Registry:
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0 WITH**:
  1. Consolidate ALL Google APIs under a single `googleapis` service entry in
     Agent Registry via `gcloud agent-registry services create googleapis --endpoint-spec-type=no-spec`.
  2. Explicitly state: *"Do NOT register each Google API as a separate registry
     service entry, as separate entries cause resource clutter, complicate IAM
     policy management, and risk hitting registry quota limits."*
  3. List all 8 required base FQDN interfaces (plus global
     `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com` when calling global Gemini models):
     - `https://agentregistry.googleapis.com`
     - `https://aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://cloudresourcemanager.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://iamcredentials.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://{region}-aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`
     - `https://aiplatform.{region}.rep.googleapis.com`
  4. Refer to `references/agent-registry.md` §2 for the full command.

### Rule 4: Cloud Run / Cloud Functions Egress 401/403 (OIDC vs IAP MCP)
If an agent gets a `401` or `403` egress error calling an MCP server or tool on
Cloud Run or Cloud Functions:
- **DO NOT RUN LOG TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0 WITH**:
  1. Explain that direct Agent Identity (`principalSet://...` / `principal://...`)
     to standard Cloud Run OIDC authentication is **not natively supported**.
  2. Recommend **Service Account impersonation** in agent code to obtain an OIDC
     ID token, granting **`roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`** to the Agent
     Identity on the target SA (and `roles/run.invoker` to that SA on Cloud Run).
  3. Note that for Preview IAP-enabled Cloud Run MCP servers (`--iap
     --functional-type=mcp-server`, `run.app` short URL), authorize via IAP/UAP
     instead of `roles/run.invoker` (see `references/known-issues.md` BKI 21 and
     `references/agent-identity.md`).

### Rule 5: Telemetry & Monitoring Endpoint Blocks on Startup
If Agent Runtime startup crashes (`set_up()`) with connection resets or
handshake errors reaching `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`:
- **Evidence**: Explicitly check whether all 4 monitoring/tracing endpoints are
  registered as Endpoints in Agent Registry (`gcloud agent-registry endpoints list`):
  `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`, `monitoring.googleapis.com`,
  `trace.mtls.googleapis.com`, and `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`.
- **Recommended Fix**:
  1. Register missing telemetry/tracing interfaces via `gcloud agent-registry
     services create --endpoint-spec-type=no-spec` (which projects read-only
     Endpoints in Agent Registry for `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`,
     `monitoring.googleapis.com`, `trace.mtls.googleapis.com`, and
     `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`).
  2. Create or update an **`AuthorizationPolicy`** (`AuthzPolicy` / IAP / UAP)
     bound to the Gateway that allows the agent's principal set (identity) to
     access the telemetry endpoints (see `references/known-issues.md` BKI 23).

### Rule 6: IAP Denial Troubleshooting (`403` / `Egress request is not authorized`)
When logs or symptoms show `403` / `Egress request is not authorized` via IAP:
1. **Check IAP Egressor bindings on the registry entry FIRST** (`roles/iap.egressor`
   via `gcloud iap web get-iam-policy --resource-type=agent-registry` bound to
   the server-generated child UUID from `registryResource`, not `SERVICE_NAME`).
2. **Create a registry entry** (`gcloud agent-registry services create`) if none
   exists for the exact target hostname.
3. **Grant `roles/iap.egressor`** on the registry entry (IAM v1 — `set-iam-policy` requires top-level `{"bindings": [...]}` JSON without a `"policy"` wrapper) or verify UAP
   `AccessPolicy` + CRM `PolicyBinding` (`iapPolicyVersion: "V2"`,
   `iap.googleapis.com/resources.egressViaIAP`; see `references/policies.md` §2).
4. **Check IAP audit logs** (`protoPayload.serviceName="iap.googleapis.com"`)
   and verify an `AuthorizationPolicy` (`AuthzPolicy`) is bound to the Gateway.
5. **Explicitly warn**: *"Do NOT use `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` (which
   is for classic IAP TCP tunneling to GCE VMs, not Agent Gateway egress) and do
   NOT bypass IAP authentication."*

### Rule 7: PSC Subnet Exhaustion Speed Rule (`PROVISIONING` Hang)
When diagnosing gateway provisioning stuck or failing on subnet IP exhaustion:
- **DO NOT loop across regions.** Run ONLY in the target region (default `us-central1`):
  1. `gcloud network-services agent-gateways list --location=us-central1`
  2. `gcloud network-services agent-gateways describe <GW> --location=us-central1`
  3. `gcloud compute network-attachments describe <NA> --region=us-central1`
  4. `gcloud compute networks subnets describe <SUBNET> --region=us-central1`
- Check free IP count (`Usable - Allocated = Free`) **before** recommending any
  Network Attachment deletion; flag that a `/28` subnet is easily exhausted and
  recommend expanding the CIDR range to at least `/26` (`known-issues.md` BKI 19).

### Rule 8: Multi-Region Manual Registration Prohibition (`us` / `eu`)
If asked about manually registering endpoints or services in `us` or `eu`:
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0**:
  1. *"Manual endpoint/service registration is NOT supported in `us` or `eu`
     multi-region locations (`us` and `eu` are read-only roll-up locations for
     auto-discovered resources)."* (Explicitly name BOTH `us` and `eu`.)
  2. *"Register manually in a specific region (e.g., `us-central1`) or `global`."*

### Rule 9: VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC) Perimeter & ACT `ALL_TRAFFIC`
When diagnosing VPC-SC perimeter blocks or external API hangs under VPC-SC:
1. Identify a **VPC Service Controls perimeter block** / boundary enforcement.
2. Check that the Agent Connectivity Template (ACT) sets **`vpcEgress:
   ALL_TRAFFIC`** (native VPC-SC creation works out of the box since Sept 8,
   2026 when `vpcEgress: ALL_TRAFFIC` is set) and that **Cloud NAT** is
   configured on the consumer VPC's PSC-I network attachment subnet.
3. For legacy or strict custom perimeters blocking Google actuation identities,
   recommend creating **ingress policies** allowing:
   - `actuation-a@networkservices-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
   - `cloud-aiplatform-pipeline-robot-prod@system.gserviceaccount.com`
4. Explicitly state: *"Do NOT disable VPC Service Controls or delete perimeters."*
   Refer to `references/known-issues.md` BKI 18 & 28.

### Rule 10: UAP Policy Binding Org Policy Blocker & Blanket `DENY` Crash
- **`CUSTOM_ORG_POLICY_VIOLATION` on `gcloud iam policy-bindings create`**:
  Caused by **`constraints/iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBinding`** (note: some
  docs misspell this plural). Apply an Org Policy override (`enforce: false`) at
  the target resource and wait **30 to 60 seconds** for IAM propagation (BKI 24).
- **Startup crash after UAP `destination.is_registered == false` `DENY`**:
  Explain that the blanket `DENY` blocked internal/unauthenticated SDK bootstrap
  and metadata calls (such as Cloud Resource Manager project lookups) during
  Reasoning Engine init; remove or scope the blanket `DENY` rule (BKI 5).

### Rule 11: Agent Gateway Dual-Registry & Jurisdiction Invariants
When configuring or validating `registries` on an Agent Gateway:
1. An Agent Gateway supports a **maximum of two registries**.
2. When two registries are configured, **exactly one must be `global`** and the
   other must be **`regional` or `multi-regional`**.
3. Binding two regional registries (e.g., `us-central1` + `europe-west1`), two
   multi-regionals, two globals, or a mismatched jurisdiction (e.g., `us-central1`
   gateway + `eu` registry) is invalid and rejected with an **HTTP 400**
   validation error (`references/agent-gateway.md` §4, BKI 26).

### Rule 12: Cross-Project Runtime-to-Gateway Binding Diagnosis
When Reasoning Engine in Project 1 fails to bind to a Gateway in Project 2:
1. **Deploying Identity**: Needs `networkservices.agentGateways.use` and
   `networkservices.agentGateways.get` (or `roles/networkservices.viewer`) in Project 2.
2. **Vertex AI Service Agent**: Grant `roles/networkservices.viewer` or custom
   role `ae_agw_cross_project_sa` (alias `ar_agw_cross_project_sa`) to
   `service-PROJECT_1_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in Project 2.
3. **Regional Colocation**: Verify both runtime and gateway are in the **same region**.
4. **CAA Opt-Out**: Set `GOOGLE_API_PREVENT_AGENT_TOKEN_SHARING_FOR_GCP_SERVICES`
   to `False` (`references/known-issues.md` BKI 10, `references/agent-gateway.md` §11).

### Rule 13: Downstream SWP + PBR vs. Explicit Forward HTTPS Proxy
Distinguish the two supported consumer-VPC proxy architectures:
- **Pattern A — Transparent Next-Hop SWP + PBR** (no client `HTTPS_PROXY` needed):
  1. Explain that **PSC endpoints cannot be route next-hops**, **SWP behind PSC
     Service Attachments only supports explicit proxy mode (not transparent
     next-hop mode)**, and **static routes cannot be used because Network
     Attachments cannot have VM network tags**.
  2. Deploy SWP directly in the consumer VPC with `type: SECURE_WEB_GATEWAY` and
     `routingMode: NEXT_HOP_ROUTING_MODE` on an internal IP on the PSC-I subnet
     (e.g., `10.20.1.250`), with a `/26` `REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY` `ACTIVE` subnet.
  3. Configure **Policy-Based Routing (PBR)** matching source CIDR `10.20.1.0/24`
     to `--next-hop-ilb-ip=10.20.1.250` (priority 200) + fallback PBR (1000).
  4. Create **Cloud NAT with `ENDPOINT_TYPE_SWG`** (`nats create ... --endpoint-types=ENDPOINT_TYPE_VM,ENDPOINT_TYPE_SWG`),
     and allowlist `<region>-aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com` in SWP CEL (BKI 33).
- **Pattern B — Explicit Forward HTTPS Proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY` + L4 `AuthzPolicy`)**:
  1. Without L4 bypass, `HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.corp.internal:443` fails on
     `HTTP CONNECT` with **HTTP `404`** because Agent Gateway's L7 HTTP manager
     terminates TLS and rejects nested `CONNECT`.
  2. Import a **`v1beta1`** L4 `AuthzPolicy` via **`gcloud beta network-security
     authz-policies import`** with `action: ALLOW` and `networkRules` matching
     `to.operations[].snis` (omit `target.loadBalancingScheme` and `ports`; max 5 rules;
     omit `from` or include `7.0.0.0/8` + PSC-I CIDR in `from.sources[].ipBlocks`).
  3. Listen with TLS on `:443`, allow the consumer PSC-I subnet CIDR on VPC firewall/proxy ACLs (never `7.0.0.0/8`),
     set `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` to `.googleapis.com,googleapis.com,metadata.google.internal,169.254.169.254,localhost,127.0.0.1`,
     bundle `agentGatewayCard.rootCertificates` + Private CA in container env
     vars (`SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`), and warn L4 `ALLOW` bypasses
     L7 IAP/UAP, Model Armor, SGP, and `httpRules` for matched SNIs (BKI 34).

### Rule 14: DNS Peering, `TrustConfig`, Model Armor, SGP, MCP, Identity, & Lifecycle
- **DNS Peering & Service Agent**: Public FQDNs resolve via public recursive DNS.
  Private DNS requires `dnsPeeringConfig` (`domains` array with trailing `.`; ACT
  uses string `targetNetwork` only, whereas inline `AgentGateway.networkConfig.dnsPeeringConfig`
  also requires `targetProject`). Cloud DNS caps total peering hops at **2**
  (Gateway consumes Hop 1 → max 1 consumer peering hop; a 2nd hop fails preflight
  or returns `SERVFAIL` → `503`, BKI 35). Grant `roles/dns.peer`, `roles/dns.reader`,
  `roles/compute.networkViewer`, and `roles/compute.networkUser` to
  `service-GATEWAY_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
  (and `compute.networkAttachments.use` to caller, BKI 9). Never use authoritative `"."` private root zones (`"."` requires a Cloud DNS Private Forwarding Zone).
- **Private CA `TrustConfig` & Immutable ACT**: Set `egressNetworkConfig.tlsConfig.trustConfig`
  **with `additionalRoots: PUBLICLY_TRUSTED_ROOTS`** (omitting breaks `*.googleapis.com`).
  ACT fields are immutable — create a new ACT and rebind via `PATCH` with
  `updateMask=agentConnectivityTemplate` (BKI 6).
- **Model Armor (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`)**: Ingress (`CLIENT_TO_AGENT`, max 1, ADK
  `streamQuery` only) uses `service-AGENT_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform-re.iam.gserviceaccount.com`;
  Egress (`AGENT_TO_ANYWHERE`, max 4) uses `service-GATEWAY_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-dep.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
  Scope `httpRules` `when` to exclude gRPC and streams **>60 seconds** (`Stream removed`, BKI 13).
- **Semantic Governance Policies (SGP)**: Uses `gcp-sa-aiplatform`, non-streaming
  LLM calls only, `.contains()` + `!request.headers['content-type'].startsWith('application/grpc')`
  in `when`, and full-map updates on `PATCH ?updateMask=metadata` so
  `sgpEnforcementMode: "DRY_RUN"` and `sgpUserIntentMatching` are preserved (BKI 38).
- **Native MCP, Identity, Trace, & Teardown**: Set `baseProtocolMethodsOption:
  MATCH_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS` on MCP `ALLOW` rules (BKI 39). Orgless trust
  domains use `agents.global.proj-PROJECT_NUMBER.system.id.goog` (`proj-`, never
  `project-`); never grant `roles/aiplatform.expressUser` or project-wide
  `roles/aiplatform.user` to Agent Identities. For Cloud Trace (`TelemetryPolicy`),
  always recommend enabling `cloudtrace.googleapis.com` (`gcloud services enable cloudtrace.googleapis.com`)
  and granting `roles/cloudtrace.agent` to `compute-system`, `gcp-sa-networksecurity`,
  and `gcp-sa-agentgateway` (see `references/agent-gateway.md` §8.3 and `references/field-manual.md` Step 14.4). Tear down in strict 7-step order
  (workloads → UAP bindings → `AuthzPolicy` → extensions → `AgentGateway` → ACT →
  VPC) and use unique gateway IDs if deletion tombstones collide (BKIs 25, 30).

## Quick Symptom Triage Matrix

| Symptom / Error | Primary Suspect | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `403` / `Egress request is not authorized` | Unregistered FQDN, missing `roles/iap.egressor` / UAP binding, or PAB | Rules 4, 6; `references/policies.md` §2; BKIs 4, 7, 8, 15 |
| `HTTP 404` on `HTTP CONNECT` (`HTTPS_PROXY`) | Missing `gcloud beta` L4 `AuthzPolicy` (`networkRules` `snis`) | Rule 13B; `references/agent-gateway.md` §6.3; BKI 34 |
| `HTTP 498` immediately after binding runtime | Enforcing gateway bound before allowlisting essential platform APIs | `references/agent-gateway.md` §2; BKI 37 |
| `500` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `Stream removed` | Model Armor SA roles (`gcp-sa-dep` vs `gcp-sa-aiplatform-re`) or 60s stream cap | Rule 14; `references/policies.md` §12; BKI 13 |
| `503` / `NXDOMAIN` / `SERVFAIL` on private host | >2-hop DNS peering, authoritative `"."` zone, Packet Intercept, or SWP | Rules 13A, 14; `references/agent-gateway.md` §3, §6; BKIs 33, 35, 36 |
| `Config validation failed` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` on import | Disabled `agentregistry.googleapis.com`, missing caller/`gcp-sa-agentgateway` IAM, or bad NA URI | Rule 14; BKIs 9, 20, 26 |
| `HTTP 409 ABORTED` / `400 already being used` | Active control-plane LRO mutex (~2 min), tombstone collision, or reverse teardown | `references/agent-gateway.md` §9, §10; BKIs 25, 29, 30 |
| Startup crash (`reasoning_engine_stderr`) | Blocked telemetry/CRM bootstrap, UAP blanket `DENY`, or SGP gRPC interception | Rules 5, 10, 14; BKIs 1, 5, 17, 23, 38 |

## When to use this skill

Trigger on Agent Gateway, Agent Connectivity Templates (ACT), Agent Registry,
Agent Identity, IAP/UAP policies, Model Armor, Semantic Governance Policies
(SGP), SWP/Explicit Proxy egress, Private CA `TrustConfig`, Cloud DNS peering,
Cloud Trace `TelemetryPolicy`, or Gemini Enterprise / Agent Runtime / GKE /
Cloud Run gateway bindings. Do **not** use for generic Google Cloud IAM, GCS,
GCE, or networking issues unrelated to the Agent Platform stack.

## Required context & Hypothesis Rules

Gather `PROJECT_ID`, `PROJECT_NUMBER`, `LOCATION` (default `us-central1`),
`AGENT_ID`, `AGENT_GATEWAY_NAME`, Agent Identity (`principal://` or
`principalSet://`), exact error + timestamp, and target destination. If missing,
ask or state unknowns using placeholders — never scan across projects or loop
over regions. Before Step 1 queries, formulate **at most 3 hypotheses** anchored
to *"Why did it start failing now?"* (e.g., recent Terraform/config changes).

## Diagnostic flow

Follow in order (copy-paste commands in `references/field-manual.md`):
- **Step 0 — Pre-Flight & Access**: Evaluate Rules 1–14. Verify project access
  (`gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID`).
- **Step 1 — Agent & Startup Logs**: Classify error (`403`, `404 CONNECT`, `498`,
  `500`, `503`, crash, timeout). Check PSC subnet IPs, ACT `ALL_TRAFFIC` + Cloud
  NAT, and `agentGatewayCard.rootCertificates` CA trust.
- **Step 2 — Gateway Logs**: Query `networkservices.googleapis.com/Gateway`
  (filtering `-httpRequest.requestMethod="CONNECT"` when inspecting L7 requests)
  to find the exact failing SNI/hostname and `serviceExtensionsInfo`.
- **Step 3 — IAP / Model Armor / SGP Logs**: Check `iapPolicyVersion` (`V1` vs
  `V2`), `DRY_RUN` vs enforced, Model Armor callout status, or
  `logs/semantic-governance-policy` verdicts and rationales.
- **Step 4 — Registry State**: Verify exact hostname permutations in
  `gcloud agent-registry {services,endpoints,mcp-servers,agents} list` and
  confirm dual-registry + jurisdiction rules.
- **Step 5 — Identity & Policies**: Check `roles/iap.egressor` via
  `--resource-type=agent-registry` on the child UUID (V1), UAP
  `AccessPolicy`/`PolicyBinding` + `constraints/iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBinding`
  (V2), PAB overrides, and least-privilege Agent Identity roles (`proj-` for orgless).
- **Step 6 — AuthzPolicy & Extensions**: Verify L4 `networkRules` vs L7
  `httpRules`, MCP `MATCH_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS`, Model Armor / SGP `when`
  exclusions, `ExtensionBinding` scope, and policy caps (max 4 egress, max 1 ingress `CONTENT_AUTHZ`).
- **Step 7 — Connectivity, DNS, & TLS**: Verify ACT `TrustConfig`
  (`PUBLICLY_TRUSTED_ROOTS`), `gcp-sa-agentgateway` IAM, <=2 DNS peering hops,
  no Packet Intercept on the consumer VPC, and SWP/Explicit Proxy settings.
- **Step 8 — PrincipalSet & Trace Verification**: Test 1:1 `principal://`
  binding if `principalSet://` lags; for Cloud Trace, enable `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`, verify `v1beta1` `TelemetryPolicy` (`telemetryTarget` referencing `agentGateways/*` and object `parentBasedSampling: {enabled: true, samplingRate: 1.0}`, never string `ENABLED`), and grant `roles/cloudtrace.agent` to `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-networksecurity.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, and `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

### Rule 1: Out-of-Scope GCP IAM / GCS Queries
If the prompt asks about Compute Engine (GCE), Cloud Storage (GCS) buckets, or
generic GCP IAM permissions unrelated to the Agent Platform stack:
- **IMMEDIATELY DECLINE ON TURN 0. DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS OR GIVE IAM GUIDES.**
- Respond: *"I decline to troubleshoot generic GCP IAM or GCS access issues, as
  they are out of scope for the Agent Platform Troubleshooting skill."*

### Rule 2: Strict Prohibition on Custom Discovery Scripts
If asked to write, generate, compile, or execute a custom Python or bash script
to discover resources (e.g., active Agent Runtime instances):
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS OR WRITE/RUN ANY SCRIPTS.**
- **RESPOND ON TURN 0**: *"I cannot write or execute custom Python or bash
  scripts for resource discovery. Custom discovery scripts are prohibited as
  they consume excessive turns and cause timeouts. Instead, use standard gcloud
  CLI commands (see [Google Cloud SDK Installation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk.md.txt))
  or curl REST API calls with application default credentials:
  `gcloud agent-registry agents list --location=us-central1` or `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" "https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines"`"*

### Rule 3: Consolidated Registry for Google APIs / Design Queries
If asked about registering multiple Agent Runtime, Cloud Resource Manager, or
Google API interfaces, or structuring services in Agent Registry:
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0 WITH**:
  1. Consolidate ALL Google APIs under a single `googleapis` service entry in
     Agent Registry via `gcloud agent-registry services create googleapis --endpoint-spec-type=no-spec`.
  2. Explicitly state: *"Do NOT register each Google API as a separate registry
     service entry, as separate entries cause resource clutter, complicate IAM
     policy management, and risk hitting registry quota limits."*
  3. List all 8 required base FQDN interfaces (plus global
     `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com` when calling global Gemini models):
     - `https://agentregistry.googleapis.com`
     - `https://aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://cloudresourcemanager.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://iamcredentials.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://{region}-aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com`
     - `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`
     - `https://aiplatform.{region}.rep.googleapis.com`
  4. Refer to `references/agent-registry.md` §2 for the full command.

### Rule 4: Cloud Run / Cloud Functions Egress 401/403 (OIDC vs IAP MCP)
If an agent gets a `401` or `403` egress error calling an MCP server or tool on
Cloud Run or Cloud Functions:
- **DO NOT RUN LOG TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0 WITH**:
  1. Explain that direct Agent Identity (`principalSet://...` / `principal://...`)
     to standard Cloud Run OIDC authentication is **not natively supported**.
  2. Recommend **Service Account impersonation** in agent code to obtain an OIDC
     ID token, granting **`roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`** to the Agent
     Identity on the target SA (and `roles/run.invoker` to that SA on Cloud Run).
  3. Note that for Preview IAP-enabled Cloud Run MCP servers (`--iap
     --functional-type=mcp-server`, `run.app` short URL), authorize via IAP/UAP
     instead of `roles/run.invoker` (see `references/known-issues.md` BKI 21 and
     `references/agent-identity.md`).

### Rule 5: Telemetry & Monitoring Endpoint Blocks on Startup
If Agent Runtime startup crashes (`set_up()`) with connection resets or
handshake errors reaching `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`:
- **Evidence**: Explicitly check whether all 4 monitoring/tracing endpoints are
  registered as Endpoints in Agent Registry (`gcloud agent-registry endpoints list`):
  `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`, `monitoring.googleapis.com`,
  `trace.mtls.googleapis.com`, and `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`.
- **Recommended Fix**:
  1. Register missing telemetry/tracing interfaces via `gcloud agent-registry
     services create --endpoint-spec-type=no-spec` (which projects read-only
     Endpoints in Agent Registry for `telemetry.mtls.googleapis.com`,
     `monitoring.googleapis.com`, `trace.mtls.googleapis.com`, and
     `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`).
  2. Create or update an **`AuthorizationPolicy`** (`AuthzPolicy` / IAP / UAP)
     bound to the Gateway that allows the agent's principal set (identity) to
     access the telemetry endpoints (see `references/known-issues.md` BKI 23).

### Rule 6: IAP Denial Troubleshooting (`403` / `Egress request is not authorized`)
When logs or symptoms show `403` / `Egress request is not authorized` via IAP:
1. **Check IAP Egressor bindings on the registry entry FIRST** (`roles/iap.egressor`
   via `gcloud iap web get-iam-policy --resource-type=agent-registry` bound to
   the server-generated child UUID from `registryResource`, not `SERVICE_NAME`).
2. **Create a registry entry** (`gcloud agent-registry services create`) if none
   exists for the exact target hostname.
3. **Grant `roles/iap.egressor`** on the registry entry (IAM v1 — `set-iam-policy` requires top-level `{"bindings": [...]}` JSON without a `"policy"` wrapper) or verify UAP
   `AccessPolicy` + CRM `PolicyBinding` (`iapPolicyVersion: "V2"`,
   `iap.googleapis.com/resources.egressViaIAP`; see `references/policies.md` §2).
4. **Check IAP audit logs** (`protoPayload.serviceName="iap.googleapis.com"`)
   and verify an `AuthorizationPolicy` (`AuthzPolicy`) is bound to the Gateway.
5. **Explicitly warn**: *"Do NOT use `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` (which
   is for classic IAP TCP tunneling to GCE VMs, not Agent Gateway egress) and do
   NOT bypass IAP authentication."*

### Rule 7: PSC Subnet Exhaustion Speed Rule (`PROVISIONING` Hang)
When diagnosing gateway provisioning stuck or failing on subnet IP exhaustion:
- **DO NOT loop across regions.** Run ONLY in the target region (default `us-central1`):
  1. `gcloud network-services agent-gateways list --location=us-central1`
  2. `gcloud network-services agent-gateways describe <GW> --location=us-central1`
  3. `gcloud compute network-attachments describe <NA> --region=us-central1`
  4. `gcloud compute networks subnets describe <SUBNET> --region=us-central1`
- Check free IP count (`Usable - Allocated = Free`) **before** recommending any
  Network Attachment deletion; flag that a `/28` subnet is easily exhausted and
  recommend expanding the CIDR range to at least `/26` (`known-issues.md` BKI 19).

### Rule 8: Multi-Region Manual Registration Prohibition (`us` / `eu`)
If asked about manually registering endpoints or services in `us` or `eu`:
- **DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS. RESPOND ON TURN 0**:
  1. *"Manual endpoint/service registration is NOT supported in `us` or `eu`
     multi-region locations (`us` and `eu` are read-only roll-up locations for
     auto-discovered resources)."* (Explicitly name BOTH `us` and `eu`.)
  2. *"Register manually in a specific region (e.g., `us-central1`) or `global`."*

### Rule 9: VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC) Perimeter & ACT `ALL_TRAFFIC`
When diagnosing VPC-SC perimeter blocks or external API hangs under VPC-SC:
1. Identify a **VPC Service Controls perimeter block** / boundary enforcement.
2. Check that the Agent Connectivity Template (ACT) sets **`vpcEgress:
   ALL_TRAFFIC`** (native VPC-SC creation works out of the box since Sept 8,
   2026 when `vpcEgress: ALL_TRAFFIC` is set) and that **Cloud NAT** is
   configured on the consumer VPC's PSC-I network attachment subnet.
3. For legacy or strict custom perimeters blocking Google actuation identities,
   recommend creating **ingress policies** allowing:
   - `actuation-a@networkservices-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
   - `cloud-aiplatform-pipeline-robot-prod@system.gserviceaccount.com`
4. Explicitly state: *"Do NOT disable VPC Service Controls or delete perimeters."*
   Refer to `references/known-issues.md` BKI 18 & 28.

### Rule 10: UAP Policy Binding Org Policy Blocker & Blanket `DENY` Crash
- **`CUSTOM_ORG_POLICY_VIOLATION` on `gcloud iam policy-bindings create`**:
  Caused by **`constraints/iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBinding`** (note: some
  docs misspell this plural). Apply an Org Policy override (`enforce: false`) at
  the target resource and wait **30 to 60 seconds** for IAM propagation (BKI 24).
- **Startup crash after UAP `destination.is_registered == false` `DENY`**:
  Explain that the blanket `DENY` blocked internal/unauthenticated SDK bootstrap
  and metadata calls (such as Cloud Resource Manager project lookups) during
  Reasoning Engine init; remove or scope the blanket `DENY` rule (BKI 5).

### Rule 11: Agent Gateway Dual-Registry & Jurisdiction Invariants
When configuring or validating `registries` on an Agent Gateway:
1. An Agent Gateway supports a **maximum of two registries**.
2. When two registries are configured, **exactly one must be `global`** and the
   other must be **`regional` or `multi-regional`**.
3. Binding two regional registries (e.g., `us-central1` + `europe-west1`), two
   multi-regionals, two globals, or a mismatched jurisdiction (e.g., `us-central1`
   gateway + `eu` registry) is invalid and rejected with an **HTTP 400**
   validation error (`references/agent-gateway.md` §4, BKI 26).

### Rule 12: Cross-Project Runtime-to-Gateway Binding Diagnosis
When Reasoning Engine in Project 1 fails to bind to a Gateway in Project 2:
1. **Deploying Identity**: Needs `networkservices.agentGateways.use` and
   `networkservices.agentGateways.get` (or `roles/networkservices.viewer`) in Project 2.
2. **Vertex AI Service Agent**: Grant `roles/networkservices.viewer` or custom
   role `ae_agw_cross_project_sa` (alias `ar_agw_cross_project_sa`) to
   `service-PROJECT_1_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com` in Project 2.
3. **Regional Colocation**: Verify both runtime and gateway are in the **same region**.
4. **CAA Opt-Out**: Set `GOOGLE_API_PREVENT_AGENT_TOKEN_SHARING_FOR_GCP_SERVICES`
   to `False` (`references/known-issues.md` BKI 10, `references/agent-gateway.md` §11).

### Rule 13: Downstream SWP + PBR vs. Explicit Forward HTTPS Proxy
Distinguish the two supported consumer-VPC proxy architectures:
- **Pattern A — Transparent Next-Hop SWP + PBR** (no client `HTTPS_PROXY` needed):
  1. Explain that **PSC endpoints cannot be route next-hops**, **SWP behind PSC
     Service Attachments only supports explicit proxy mode (not transparent
     next-hop mode)**, and **static routes cannot be used because Network
     Attachments cannot have VM network tags**.
  2. Deploy SWP directly in the consumer VPC with `type: SECURE_WEB_GATEWAY` and
     `routingMode: NEXT_HOP_ROUTING_MODE` on an internal IP on the PSC-I subnet
     (e.g., `10.20.1.250`), with a `/26` `REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY` `ACTIVE` subnet.
  3. Configure **Policy-Based Routing (PBR)** matching source CIDR `10.20.1.0/24`
     to `--next-hop-ilb-ip=10.20.1.250` (priority 200) + fallback PBR (1000).
  4. Create **Cloud NAT with `ENDPOINT_TYPE_SWG`** (`nats create ... --endpoint-types=ENDPOINT_TYPE_VM,ENDPOINT_TYPE_SWG`),
     and allowlist `<region>-aiplatform.mtls.googleapis.com` in SWP CEL (BKI 33).
- **Pattern B — Explicit Forward HTTPS Proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY` + L4 `AuthzPolicy`)**:
  1. Without L4 bypass, `HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.corp.internal:443` fails on
     `HTTP CONNECT` with **HTTP `404`** because Agent Gateway's L7 HTTP manager
     terminates TLS and rejects nested `CONNECT`.
  2. Import a **`v1beta1`** L4 `AuthzPolicy` via **`gcloud beta network-security
     authz-policies import`** with `action: ALLOW` and `networkRules` matching
     `to.operations[].snis` (omit `target.loadBalancingScheme` and `ports`; max 5 rules;
     omit `from` or include `7.0.0.0/8` + PSC-I CIDR in `from.sources[].ipBlocks`).
  3. Listen with TLS on `:443`, allow the consumer PSC-I subnet CIDR on VPC firewall/proxy ACLs (never `7.0.0.0/8`),
     set `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` to `.googleapis.com,googleapis.com,metadata.google.internal,169.254.169.254,localhost,127.0.0.1`,
     bundle `agentGatewayCard.rootCertificates` + Private CA in container env
     vars (`SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`), and warn L4 `ALLOW` bypasses
     L7 IAP/UAP, Model Armor, SGP, and `httpRules` for matched SNIs (BKI 34).

### Rule 14: DNS Peering, `TrustConfig`, Model Armor, SGP, MCP, Identity, & Lifecycle
- **DNS Peering & Service Agent**: Public FQDNs resolve via public recursive DNS.
  Private DNS requires `dnsPeeringConfig` (`domains` array with trailing `.`; ACT
  uses string `targetNetwork` only, whereas inline `AgentGateway.networkConfig.dnsPeeringConfig`
  also requires `targetProject`). Cloud DNS caps total peering hops at **2**
  (Gateway consumes Hop 1 → max 1 consumer peering hop; a 2nd hop fails preflight
  or returns `SERVFAIL` → `503`, BKI 35). Grant `roles/dns.peer`, `roles/dns.reader`,
  `roles/compute.networkViewer`, and `roles/compute.networkUser` to
  `service-GATEWAY_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
  (and `compute.networkAttachments.use` to caller, BKI 9). Never use authoritative `"."` private root zones (`"."` requires a Cloud DNS Private Forwarding Zone).
- **Private CA `TrustConfig` & Immutable ACT**: Set `egressNetworkConfig.tlsConfig.trustConfig`
  **with `additionalRoots: PUBLICLY_TRUSTED_ROOTS`** (omitting breaks `*.googleapis.com`).
  ACT fields are immutable — create a new ACT and rebind via `PATCH` with
  `updateMask=agentConnectivityTemplate` (BKI 6).
- **Model Armor (`CONTENT_AUTHZ`)**: Ingress (`CLIENT_TO_AGENT`, max 1, ADK
  `streamQuery` only) uses `service-AGENT_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform-re.iam.gserviceaccount.com`;
  Egress (`AGENT_TO_ANYWHERE`, max 4) uses `service-GATEWAY_PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-dep.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
  Scope `httpRules` `when` to exclude gRPC and streams **>60 seconds** (`Stream removed`, BKI 13).
- **Semantic Governance Policies (SGP)**: Uses `gcp-sa-aiplatform`, non-streaming
  LLM calls only, `.contains()` + `!request.headers['content-type'].startsWith('application/grpc')`
  in `when`, and full-map updates on `PATCH ?updateMask=metadata` so
  `sgpEnforcementMode: "DRY_RUN"` and `sgpUserIntentMatching` are preserved (BKI 38).
- **Native MCP, Identity, Trace, & Teardown**: Set `baseProtocolMethodsOption:
  MATCH_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS` on MCP `ALLOW` rules (BKI 39). Orgless trust
  domains use `agents.global.proj-PROJECT_NUMBER.system.id.goog` (`proj-`, never
  `project-`); never grant `roles/aiplatform.expressUser` or project-wide
  `roles/aiplatform.user` to Agent Identities. For Cloud Trace (`TelemetryPolicy`),
  always recommend enabling `cloudtrace.googleapis.com` (`gcloud services enable cloudtrace.googleapis.com`)
  and granting `roles/cloudtrace.agent` to `compute-system`, `gcp-sa-networksecurity`,
  and `gcp-sa-agentgateway` (see `references/agent-gateway.md` §8.3 and `references/field-manual.md` Step 14.4). Tear down in strict 7-step order
  (workloads → UAP bindings → `AuthzPolicy` → extensions → `AgentGateway` → ACT →
  VPC) and use unique gateway IDs if deletion tombstones collide (BKIs 25, 30).

## Quick Symptom Triage Matrix

| Symptom / Error | Primary Suspect | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `403` / `Egress request is not authorized` | Unregistered FQDN, missing `roles/iap.egressor` / UAP binding, or PAB | Rules 4, 6; `references/policies.md` §2; BKIs 4, 7, 8, 15 |
| `HTTP 404` on `HTTP CONNECT` (`HTTPS_PROXY`) | Missing `gcloud beta` L4 `AuthzPolicy` (`networkRules` `snis`) | Rule 13B; `references/agent-gateway.md` §6.3; BKI 34 |
| `HTTP 498` immediately after binding runtime | Enforcing gateway bound before allowlisting essential platform APIs | `references/agent-gateway.md` §2; BKI 37 |
| `500` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `Stream removed` | Model Armor SA roles (`gcp-sa-dep` vs `gcp-sa-aiplatform-re`) or 60s stream cap | Rule 14; `references/policies.md` §12; BKI 13 |
| `503` / `NXDOMAIN` / `SERVFAIL` on private host | >2-hop DNS peering, authoritative `"."` zone, Packet Intercept, or SWP | Rules 13A, 14; `references/agent-gateway.md` §3, §6; BKIs 33, 35, 36 |
| `Config validation failed` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` on import | Disabled `agentregistry.googleapis.com`, missing caller/`gcp-sa-agentgateway` IAM, or bad NA URI | Rule 14; BKIs 9, 20, 26 |
| `HTTP 409 ABORTED` / `400 already being used` | Active control-plane LRO mutex (~2 min), tombstone collision, or reverse teardown | `references/agent-gateway.md` §9, §10; BKIs 25, 29, 30 |
| Startup crash (`reasoning_engine_stderr`) | Blocked telemetry/CRM bootstrap, UAP blanket `DENY`, or SGP gRPC interception | Rules 5, 10, 14; BKIs 1, 5, 17, 23, 38 |

## When to use this skill

Trigger on Agent Gateway, Agent Connectivity Templates (ACT), Agent Registry,
Agent Identity, IAP/UAP policies, Model Armor, Semantic Governance Policies
(SGP), SWP/Explicit Proxy egress, Private CA `TrustConfig`, Cloud DNS peering,
Cloud Trace `TelemetryPolicy`, or Gemini Enterprise / Agent Runtime / GKE /
Cloud Run gateway bindings. Do **not** use for generic Google Cloud IAM, GCS,
GCE, or networking issues unrelated to the Agent Platform stack.

## Required context & Hypothesis Rules

Gather `PROJECT_ID`, `PROJECT_NUMBER`, `LOCATION` (default `us-central1`),
`AGENT_ID`, `AGENT_GATEWAY_NAME`, Agent Identity (`principal://` or
`principalSet://`), exact error + timestamp, and target destination. If missing,
ask or state unknowns using placeholders — never scan across projects or loop
over regions. Before Step 1 queries, formulate **at most 3 hypotheses** anchored
to *"Why did it start failing now?"* (e.g., recent Terraform/config changes).

## Diagnostic flow

Follow in order (copy-paste commands in `references/field-manual.md`):
- **Step 0 — Pre-Flight & Access**: Evaluate Rules 1–14. Verify project access
  (`gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID`).
- **Step 1 — Agent & Startup Logs**: Classify error (`403`, `404 CONNECT`, `498`,
  `500`, `503`, crash, timeout). Check PSC subnet IPs, ACT `ALL_TRAFFIC` + Cloud
  NAT, and `agentGatewayCard.rootCertificates` CA trust.
- **Step 2 — Gateway Logs**: Query `networkservices.googleapis.com/Gateway`
  (filtering `-httpRequest.requestMethod="CONNECT"` when inspecting L7 requests)
  to find the exact failing SNI/hostname and `serviceExtensionsInfo`.
- **Step 3 — IAP / Model Armor / SGP Logs**: Check `iapPolicyVersion` (`V1` vs
  `V2`), `DRY_RUN` vs enforced, Model Armor callout status, or
  `logs/semantic-governance-policy` verdicts and rationales.
- **Step 4 — Registry State**: Verify exact hostname permutations in
  `gcloud agent-registry {services,endpoints,mcp-servers,agents} list` and
  confirm dual-registry + jurisdiction rules.
- **Step 5 — Identity & Policies**: Check `roles/iap.egressor` via
  `--resource-type=agent-registry` on the child UUID (V1), UAP
  `AccessPolicy`/`PolicyBinding` + `constraints/iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBinding`
  (V2), PAB overrides, and least-privilege Agent Identity roles (`proj-` for orgless).
- **Step 6 — AuthzPolicy & Extensions**: Verify L4 `networkRules` vs L7
  `httpRules`, MCP `MATCH_BASE_PROTOCOL_METHODS`, Model Armor / SGP `when`
  exclusions, `ExtensionBinding` scope, and policy caps (max 4 egress, max 1 ingress `CONTENT_AUTHZ`).
- **Step 7 — Connectivity, DNS, & TLS**: Verify ACT `TrustConfig`
  (`PUBLICLY_TRUSTED_ROOTS`), `gcp-sa-agentgateway` IAM, <=2 DNS peering hops,
  no Packet Intercept on the consumer VPC, and SWP/Explicit Proxy settings.
- **Step 8 — PrincipalSet & Trace Verification**: Test 1:1 `principal://`
  binding if `principalSet://` lags; for Cloud Trace, enable `cloudtrace.googleapis.com`, verify `v1beta1` `TelemetryPolicy` (`telemetryTarget` referencing `agentGateways/*` and object `parentBasedSampling: {enabled: true, samplingRate: 1.0}`, never string `ENABLED`), and grant `roles/cloudtrace.agent` to `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-networksecurity.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, and `service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-agentgateway.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

## Tools & Layered References

Use `mcp__gcloud__run_gcloud_command` (or `gcloud --quiet`),

- [references/known-issues.md](references/known-issues.md) — BKIs #1–#13, #15–#39 for fast pattern matches

## Output report

Always produce a read-only diagnostic report using this exact structure:

```markdown
# Agent Platform Diagnostic — <one-line summary>

## Context
- Project: <id> (<number>) | Location: <region>
- Agent: <agent_id> | Gateway: <gateway_name>
- Symptom: <exact error message and when it started>

## Evidence gathered
- Agent log query: <filter, summary>
- Gateway log query: <filter, exact failing hostname / extension status>
- IAP / Policy log query: <filter, decision + enforcement mode>
- Registry & Policy state: <entries, AuthzPolicy bindings, roles/iap.egressor or UAP>

## Root cause hypothesis
<ranked root cause(s)>

## Why this fits the evidence
<connect log/config evidence to root cause>

## Recommended fix
<ordered gcloud / curl / YAML / Terraform changes for the user to apply>

## What to verify after the fix
<verification queries>

## Open questions / unknowns
<missing context or unverified items>

## Appendix: Raw Logs & Verified Links
- **Cloud Logging Filter**: <exact copy-pasteable filter or deep link>
- **Raw Logs**: <untruncated Agent, Gateway, and IAP/Policy log entries>
```

## Principles

- **Exact hostname match first**: Compare gateway log hostnames

# Agent Platform Tuning Management

This skill provides instructions on how to manage GenAI Tuning Jobs using the
Agent Platform Python SDK. Use this skill when a user wants to check the status
of their tuning runs, find an active tuning job, or cancel a job that is running
too long.

## Attribution

**MUST READ**: Before executing any `gcloud`, REST API, or MCP command, you MUST
read [Usage Attribution](references/attribution.md). For commands executed
directly in the terminal (never in generated scripts, Terraform, or user code),
prefix `gcloud` with `CLOUDSDK_METRICS_REQUEST_ATTRIBUTION` and append the
attribution suffix to `User-Agent` headers:

```text
CLOUDSDK_METRICS_REQUEST_ATTRIBUTION="agent-skills/1.0 (skill:agent-platform-tuning-management)"
User-Agent: <existing_user_agent> agent-skills/1.0 (skill:agent-platform-tuning-management)
```

## Safety & Confirmation Tiers (CRITICAL)

Before executing any commands on behalf of the user, you MUST adhere to the
following safety tiers based on the action requested:

1.  **Tier R: Read-only (`list`, `get`)**
    *   **Rule**: No confirmation needed. You may execute these commands
        immediately to gather information for the user.
2.  **Tier D: Destructive & Interruptive (`cancel`)**
    *   **Rule**: Cancellation is a Tier D action requiring **explicit typed
        confirmation** (e.g. "I confirm" or "Yes, cancel it").
    *   **Required Fields in Dry-Run Confirmation Card**: Before cancelling a
        tuning job, you MUST present a dry-run confirmation preview clearly
        listing:
        *   **Target Resource**: The full tuning job resource name or ID (e.g.
            `projects/<PROJECT_ID>/locations/<REGION>/tuningJobs/<JOB_ID>`).
        *   **Command / Script**: The exact cancellation command or Python code
            to be executed.
        *   **Expected Effect**: Stops the ongoing tuning job; any in-progress
            training will be halted and cannot be resumed.
        *   Ask the user to explicitly confirm (e.g., "Do you confirm? Please
            reply with 'I confirm' or 'Yes, cancel it'.").
    *   **Same-turn restriction**: NEVER execute the cancellation in the same
        turn as presenting the preview card. Stop immediately and wait for the
        user to confirm in a new turn. Even if the user provided pre-emptive
        confirmation (e.g. "Yes, I confirm, cancel tuning job ...") or provides
        a corrected job ID, you MUST present the dry-run preview for that
        specific job ID and wait for confirmation in a separate turn before
        issuing the cancellation.

## Phase 0: Environment Setup

**CRITICAL**: Before running any of the Python snippets below, you MUST ensure
the environment is correctly initialized by following these steps:

1.  **Google Cloud Authentication**: Authenticate with your Google Cloud account
    and configure active Application Default Credentials (ADC) for Agent
    Platform access:

    ```bash
    gcloud auth login
    gcloud auth application-default login
    ```

2.  **Python Dependencies**: This skill needs `google-cloud-aiplatform`. Do
    **not** create a virtual environment — it starts empty and hides packages
    the environment already provides, forcing a redundant install. Probe, and
    install only what is missing:

    ```bash
    python3 -c "import vertexai" || pip install google-cloud-aiplatform
    ```

3.  **Execution**: Run Python snippets with a plain `python3`. There is no
    environment to activate first.

## Workflow Decision Tree

1.  **Information Gathering**: Do you have a Project ID and Region?

    *   **No** -> You **MUST** ask the user for the missing Project ID and
        Region in plain text, or advise them to check their gcloud
        configuration. If neither location has this information, then ask the
        user to provide it. Do not attempt to search random regions on your own.
    *   **Yes** -> Proceed to Step 2.

2.  **Task Type**: What does the user want to do?

    *   **Find or List Jobs** -> Use the Python SDK to list tuning jobs. (Tier
        R)
    *   **Check Status / Inspect a Specific Job** -> Use the Python SDK to get
        tuning job details. (Tier R)
    *   **Cancel a Job** -> Ask for confirmation, then use the Python SDK to
        cancel the tuning job. (Tier D)

## Using the Python SDK

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Resource Verification & Missing Projects/Jobs:** If the execution of the
> Python snippet fails because of an invalid filter (e.g., `400 Provided filter
> is not valid`), fix or drop the `filter` parameter and re-run. If it fails
> with an error indicating a missing or inaccessible project or job ID (`403
> Permission Denied`, `404 Not Found`, or invalid resource ID), you **MUST**
> inform the user that the project or tuning job does not exist or cannot be
> accessed, prompt the user to provide a valid Project ID or Job ID, and stop
> tool execution immediately to wait for their response (do **NOT** loop or
> assume the resource is valid).

### 1. Listing Tuning Jobs (Tier R)

If the user asks "What tuning jobs do I have running?" or wants to find a
specific job ID, always execute Python code via `run_command` (do NOT use
`curl`). If the user gave a project ID or number, use that **exact** value
(otherwise fall back to the configured project). Pass `page_size=20` and read
the first page (only page through every job if the user explicitly asks for a
total count or the full list). Filter server-side when asked for running jobs
(`state="JOB_STATE_RUNNING" OR state="JOB_STATE_PENDING"`) or a specific model
display name (`display_name:"NAME"`), print `job.tuned_model_display_name`, and
note when `first_page.next_page_token` is set so the 20 most recently updated
jobs are not presented as the entire history:

```python
from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1

project_id = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"  # If the user gave a project ID/number, use it explicitly
region = "YOUR_REGION"
parent = f"projects/{project_id}/locations/{region}"

client = aiplatform_v1.GenAiTuningServiceClient(
    client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
)

request = {
    "parent": parent,
    "page_size": 20,
    # Optional server-side filter, e.g.:
    # "filter": 'state="JOB_STATE_RUNNING" OR state="JOB_STATE_PENDING"',
}
response = client.list_tuning_jobs(request=request)
first_page = next(iter(response.pages), None)
for job in (first_page.tuning_jobs if first_page else []):
    print(f"Name: {job.name}")
    print(f"Display Name: {job.tuned_model_display_name}")
    print(f"Base Model: {job.base_model}")
    print(f"State: {job.state.name}")
if first_page and first_page.next_page_token:
    print("Note: More jobs exist beyond this first page of 20 most recently updated jobs.")
```

### 2. Getting Details for a Specific Job (Tier R)

If the user provides a Tuning Job ID and asks for its status, always execute
Python code via `run_command` (never use `curl`). If the user gave a project ID
or number, use it explicitly:

```python
from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1

project_id = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"  # If the user gave a project ID/number, use it explicitly
region = "YOUR_REGION"
job_id = "YOUR_JOB_ID"  # 19-digit ID
name = f"projects/{project_id}/locations/{region}/tuningJobs/{job_id}"

client = aiplatform_v1.GenAiTuningServiceClient(
    client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
)

job = client.get_tuning_job(name=name)
print(f"Name: {job.name}")
print(f"Base Model: {job.base_model}")
print(f"State: {job.state.name}")
print(f"Tuning Model: {job.tuned_model_display_name}")
```

### 3. Canceling a Job (Tier D)

If the user explicitly requests to stop, abort, or cancel a tuning job:

**Safety Check**: Follow the **Tier D (Destructive / Irreversible)**
confirmation rules in the Operation Tiers section above:

-   **Never report an outcome you did not observe**: Never claim a job was
    canceled or report a backend error without actually observing it from an API
    call.
-   Present the confirmation preview with **Expected Effect** conditioned on the
    job's observed state (for active `PENDING`/`RUNNING` jobs: stops in-progress
    training, which cannot be resumed, without deleting the base model or
    dataset; if the job is already in a terminal state `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, or
    `CANCELLED`, state its current terminal state explicitly and note that no
    active training is running).
-   Wait for explicit user confirmation in a new turn before calling
    `client.cancel_tuning_job(name=name)` via Python (`run_command`), and report
    the actual API response verbatim.

```python
from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1

project_id = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"  # Use the EXACT project ID/number the user gave
region = "YOUR_REGION"
job_id = "YOUR_JOB_ID"  # 19-digit ID
name = f"projects/{project_id}/locations/{region}/tuningJobs/{job_id}"

client = aiplatform_v1.GenAiTuningServiceClient(
    client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
)

client.cancel_tuning_job(name=name)
print(f"Successfully requested cancellation for {name}")
```

**Safety Check**: Follow the **Tier D (Destructive / Irreversible)**
confirmation rules in the Operation Tiers section above:

-   **Never report an outcome you did not observe**: Never claim a job was
    canceled or report a backend error without actually observing it from an API
    call.
-   Present the confirmation preview with **Expected Effect** conditioned on the
    job's observed state (for active `PENDING`/`RUNNING` jobs: stops in-progress
    training, which cannot be resumed, without deleting the base model or
    dataset; if the job is already in a terminal state `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, or
    `CANCELLED`, state its current terminal state explicitly and note that no
    active training is running).
-   Wait for explicit user confirmation in a new turn before calling
    `client.cancel_tuning_job(name=name)` via Python (`run_command`), and report
    the actual API response verbatim.

```python
from google.cloud import aiplatform_v1

project_id = "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"  # Use the EXACT project ID/number the user gave
region = "YOUR_REGION"
job_id = "YOUR_JOB_ID"  # 19-digit ID
name = f"projects/{project_id}/locations/{region}/tuningJobs/{job_id}"

client = aiplatform_v1.GenAiTuningServiceClient(
    client_options={"api_endpoint": f"{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"}
)

client.cancel_tuning_job(name=name)
print(f"Successfully requested cancellation for {name}")
```

# Agent Platform Model Tuning

## Attribution

**MUST READ**: Before executing any `gcloud`, REST API, or MCP command, you MUST
read [Usage Attribution](references/attribution.md). For commands executed
directly in the terminal (never in generated scripts, Terraform, or user code),
prefix `gcloud` with `CLOUDSDK_METRICS_REQUEST_ATTRIBUTION` and append the
attribution suffix to `User-Agent` headers:

```text

User-Agent: <existing_user_agent> agent-skills/1.0 (skill:agent-platform-tuning)
```

## Overview

This skill provides procedural knowledge for fine-tuning Large Language Models
(both Open Models and Gemini Models) using Agent Platform's tuning service. It
covers the entire lifecycle from environment setup and data preparation to job
configuration, monitoring, and deployment.

## Workflow Decision Tree

1.  **Project & Region Verification Check**: Has the user provided the Google
    Cloud project and region?

    -   **No** → **STOP tool execution immediately**. Do NOT run verification
        commands (`gcloud services list`, `gcloud projects get-iam-policy`), do
        NOT create resources, and do NOT begin dataset preparation. Prompt the
        user to specify or confirm the project and region (e.g. "Could you
        please specify which Google Cloud project and region you would like to
        use?").
        -   If the user's inquiry is solely to check or verify environment
            readiness (APIs, IAM, service agents), ask ONLY for the project and
            region. Do NOT ask for the model category.
        -   If the user is requesting a tuning workflow and also omitted whether
            they want to tune an Open Model or a Gemini Model, you may ask both
            questions together.
    -   **Yes** → Proceed.

2.  **Model Category Identification**: Has the user explicitly stated whether
    they want to tune an **Open Model** or a **Gemini Model**?

    -   **No** →
        -   **EXCEPTION for Environment Verification Inquiries:** If the user is
            only asking to check or verify that the environment, APIs, IAM
            permissions, or service agents are ready for tuning, do NOT ask for
            the model category. Verify the environment once the project and
            region are known and confirm readiness.
        -   Otherwise, **STOP tool execution**. Ask the user if they want to
            tune an Open Model or a Gemini Model. **General Setup and
            Prerequisite Inquiries (e.g., "What environment setup is
            needed?"):** If the user asks what environment setup, prerequisites,
            APIs, or permissions are needed to start fine-tuning, and has not
            yet chosen a model category:
        *   Describe the setup requirements (APIs, IAM permissions/service
            agents, and Python SDKs).
        *   Regarding Cloud Storage: state that an existing Cloud Storage bucket
            is needed for datasets and artifacts (e.g.,
            `gs://<existing-bucket>`). **CRITICAL:** Do NOT instruct the user to
            create a bucket, do NOT output a `gcloud storage buckets create`
            command in setup instructions, and do NOT assume a non-existent
            bucket exists (users may not have bucket creation permissions and
            will provide their own existing bucket).
        *   You MUST explicitly conclude your prose response with the direct
            question: **"Would you like to tune an Open Model or a Gemini
            Model?"** (do NOT bury this choice inside a bulleted "Suggested Next
            Steps" list). Never provide setup instructions without explicitly
            asking this question in prose. (Note: if they ask to actively check
            or verify a project whose ID or region is missing, ask for the
            project and region first without running tool calls).
    -   If the user provides a specific tuning purpose, you should recommend
        three models: one Open Model, one Gemini Model, and a third generally
        recommended choice. Briefly list the pros and cons of each (e.g., Gemini
        models might be more expensive, etc.). **CRITICAL:** You must read
        `references/models.md` during this step and only recommend models
        explicitly listed in that catalog. Never recommend uncataloged or
        unsupported models like `google/gemma-2-9b-it`, `gemma-2`, or `Mistral`
        — only recommend supported models such as Gemma 3
        (`google/gemma3@gemma-3-12b-it`), Qwen 3 (`qwen/qwen3@qwen3-8b`), or
        Llama 3.1 (`meta/llama3_1@llama-3.1-8b`). For Gemini models, ONLY
        recommend `gemini-2.5-flash` (recommended for general/coding/chat) or
        `gemini-2.5-pro`. Never recommend `gemini-1.5-flash-002`,
        `gemini-1.5-pro-002`, or `gemini-1.5-flash`, which are deprecated and
        unsupported by the tuning service. If the user names a model that is not
        in the catalog, follow the fallback rule in that catalog. Do not proceed
        with model configuration until the category is confirmed.
    -   **Distillation requests**: If the user asks to distill a model, names a
        teacher model, or wants a smaller model to learn from a larger one, this
        is an Open Model workflow using distillation. Read "Distillation" in
        `references/models.md` and use only the teacher and student models
        listed there.
    -   **Yes** → Proceed.

3.  **Environment Check**: Has the environment (Auth, APIs, IAM, Venv) been
    initialized?

    -   **No** → Go to [Phase 0: Environment & IAM Setup](#phase-0).
    -   **Yes** → Proceed.

4.  **Dataset Status**: Is the dataset ready in JSONL format, **is its structure
    valid for tuning**, and is it uploaded to Google Cloud Storage?

    ```
    -   **No** → Go to [Phase 1: Dataset Preparation & Upload](#phase-1).
    -   **Yes** → Proceed.
    ```

5.  **Column Selection Confirmation**: Have you presented the columns to the
    user and confirmed the mapping?

    -   **No** → **STOP**. You must show samples and get user confirmation on
        column mapping as described in Phase 1.0 before proceeding.
    -   **Yes** → Proceed.

6.  **Configuration**: Has the user provided the target model and
    hyperparameters, or explicitly agreed to your recommendations?

    -   **No** → Go to

7.  **Job Status**: Has the tuning job been submitted?


9.  **Deployment**: Has the tuned model been deployed (if required)?

    ```
    -   **No** → Go to [Phase 5: Model Deployment](#phase-5-model-deployment).
    -   **Yes** → Task Complete.
    ```

## Phase 0: Environment & IAM Setup {#phase-0}

Ensure the foundational environment is ready before proceeding.

### 0.1 Authentication & Project Context

-   Check if `gcloud` CLI is installed. If it is not installed, prompt the user
    for permission to install it before proceeding. If it is installed, update
    it:

```bash
gcloud components update --quiet > /dev/null 2>&1
```

-   Verify `gcloud auth list`. If not authenticated, run `gcloud auth login`.
-   **Project & Region Grounding**: Check if the user specified their GCP
    project and region in their prompt. If the user's prompt omits either the
    project or the region (e.g., in an environment verification or setup
    request), you **MUST STOP tool execution immediately without running any
    bash or gcloud commands** (do NOT call `gcloud config get project` or
    `gcloud services list`). Ask the user to provide their project ID/number and
    region.
-   Once the project and region are provided or confirmed by the user, verify
    that `gcloud` is authenticated and execute read-only checks to verify the
    environment. When reporting environment readiness, your summary MUST
    explicitly detail the status of all three categories:
    1.  **Required APIs**: explicitly report that both
        `aiplatform.googleapis.com` (Agent Platform) and
        `storage.googleapis.com` (Cloud Storage) are enabled.
    2.  **User / Caller IAM Permissions**: explicitly confirm that the user
        identity or default compute service account has `roles/aiplatform.user`
        and `roles/storage.admin` (or `roles/storage.objectAdmin`).
    3.  **Service Agents & Roles**: explicitly report that the Agent Platform
        Service Agent
        (`service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) has
        `roles/aiplatform.serviceAgent`, and the Tuning Service Agent
        (`service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-vertex-moss-ft.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
        or `gcp-sa-vertex-tune`) has `roles/aiplatform.tuningServiceAgent`.
        Always explicitly state the verified project and region (e.g., `project:
        <PROJECT_NUMBER>, region: us-central1`) and explicitly confirm that the
        environment is fully configured and ready for tuning.

### 0.2 Location

Location handling **depends on the model category** you established in the
workflow decision tree. The two categories have different supported locations —
never apply one category's locations to the other.

-   **Open models** share one fixed location set, and `global` is the
    recommended choice.
-   **Gemini models** differ per model and must be looked up. `global` is not
    accepted for them today.

If the user names a location that is not valid for their model and category,
STOP. Respond with an error naming the requested location as unsupported, list
the locations that are valid, and do NOT ask for a dataset, do NOT proceed with
any other setup step, and do NOT silently retry elsewhere.

#### Open Models (RECOMMEND: `global`)

**Recommend `global` and confirm it with the user.** Propose it as a single
recommended choice rather than making the user pick a region first, and do not
steer them toward a specific region instead.

These are the only locations available for open model tuning:

-   `global` (the recommended choice)
-   `us-central1`
-   `europe-west4`
-   `us-west1`
-   `us-east5`
-   `asia-southeast1`

The `global` endpoint automatically selects a supported region that has
available capacity, so it is the most likely to be scheduled successfully.
Pinning a region up front restricts the job to that one region's capacity, which
is why `global` is the recommended location for open model tuning.

-   **The user named a location** → use it verbatim, provided it is `global` or
    one of the regions listed above. Do not talk them out of it.
-   **The user asked which locations are supported** → answer the question.
    Share the list above and say that `global` is recommended and why. Never
    withhold it.
-   **The user did not name a location** → propose `global` and ask them to
    confirm it before you proceed. Say that `global` lets the service pick a
    region with available capacity. Do NOT silently assume `global`.

The point of proposing a single choice is to avoid making region selection a
decision the user must resolve before anything else can happen — that ordering
is what previously blocked people. It is not a reason to hide the list: quote it
whenever the user asks, and quote it when rejecting an unsupported location.

Fall back to an explicit region **only** in the cases below, and tell the user
why you are doing so:

-   **CMEK.** Customer-managed encryption keys are rejected on `global` with a
    `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error. A CMEK-protected job must name the region that
    holds the key.

-   **Data residency.** If the user requires the job to stay in a specific
    jurisdiction, honor their region. `global` currently runs the job in either
    `us-central1` or `europe-west4`.

If a `global` job is accepted but then fails with a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error
saying the model does not support global endpoint tuning, that model is not
onboarded to the global endpoint yet. The model itself is still tunable:
resubmit once in an explicit region from the list above (`us-central1` is the
safest choice) and tell the user why you switched.

##### Working with a `global` job

-   The API host stays `aiplatform.googleapis.com`. There is no
    `global-aiplatform.googleapis.com` host.
-   The service resolves `global` to a real region at run time. Sub-resources
    (the tuned model, checkpoints, TensorBoard) come back with that **real**
    region in their resource names, not `global`. Read the location out of the
    returned resource name before using it for monitoring or deployment; never
    assume it is still `global`.
-   Quota is shared across regions, so pinning a region does not grant extra
    quota.

#### Gemini Models (per-model, look it up)

`global` is **not accepted for Gemini tuning today** — the service rejects it at
job creation with a `FAILED_PRECONDITION` error, so do not propose it here.

**There is no single region allowlist for Gemini.** Supported tuning regions
vary by model and by model version: some Gemini models are restricted to two
regions while others support many more. Do NOT reuse the open model list above,
and do NOT assume a region carries over from another Gemini model.

Before submitting, look up the chosen model in the supervised fine-tuning
documentation and read its **"Supported endpoint for model tuning"**
row:
[supervised tuning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/tuning/supervised-tuning)


-   **The user asked which regions are supported** → look up that specific model
    and tell them what the docs say. Do not answer from memory or from the open
    model list, and do not answer for a different Gemini model.
-   **The model's row names specific regions** → the user's region must be one
    of them. If it is not, STOP and report the supported regions for that model.
-   **The model's row is absent or the docs are unclear** → ask the user for the
    region rather than guessing one.

Confirm the region with the user before proceeding. Note that some Gemini models
also restrict CMEK and serve tuned models only on the `us` and `eu` multi-region
endpoints, so check the same table for those limits before promising them.

### 0.3 Enable APIs

Ensure `aiplatform.googleapis.com` and `storage.googleapis.com` are enabled.

```bash
gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com storage.googleapis.com \
    --project=YOUR_PROJECT
```

### 0.4 IAM Permissions

Verify the following identities have the required roles.

-   **Agent Platform Service Agent**:
    `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-aiplatform.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
-   **Managed OSS Fine Tuning Service Agent**:
    `service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-vertex-moss-ft.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
-   **User Identity**: The account running the commands.

### 0.5 Python Dependencies

The scripts in this skill import `vertexai` (from `google-cloud-aiplatform`),
`google-genai`, `google-cloud-storage`, and `datasets`.

**CRITICAL AGENT INSTRUCTION:** Do **not** create a virtual environment, and do
not install anything before checking. A venv starts empty and hides packages the
environment already provides, forcing a redundant several-minute install.

Probe first and install only if the probe fails:

```bash
python3 -c "import vertexai, google.genai, google.cloud.storage, datasets" \
  || pip install -r references/requirements.txt
```

Then run every script with a plain `python3 scripts/...` — no activation prefix.

The `references/requirements.txt` pins are a fallback for an environment that
does not already provide these SDKs. Do not apply them on top of a working
environment: they would downgrade packages other tools may share.

## Phase 1: Dataset Preparation & Upload {#phase-1}

### 1.0 Dataset Discovery & Confirmation

-   **User-Provided Dataset Verification:** If the user specifies a dataset
    filename or path in their prompt, verify its existence in the workspace
    (e.g. via script execution or checking for typos).
    *   **If the file cannot be found anywhere**, you **MUST** inform the user
        that the dataset file does not exist or cannot be accessed. You **MUST**
        prompt the user to provide a valid dataset path. Alternatively, if
        candidate dataset files are found in the workspace during your search,
        you **MUST** present the candidates to the user and ask them to select
        one. You **MUST** stop tool execution immediately after reporting the
        missing file or presenting candidates, and wait for the user's response.
        Do **NOT** ask for 90/10 validation split permission, and do **NOT**
        attempt to upload the dataset before receiving a valid dataset file
        selection from the user.
    *   **If the file is found and verified**, proceed to Step 1.1 Formatting &
        Validation below.
-   **Auto-Discovery: From User Bucket:** If the user does not have a dataset
    and no suitable alternative is found in the Hugging Face reference, offer to
    search the user's GCS buckets for potential training data. Prioritize
    searching for files with extensions like `.jsonl`, `.json`, `.csv`, and
    `.parquet`. If such files are found, read the first few lines/records of
    each to determine if they contain text-based data suitable for tuning (e.g.,
    prompt/completion pairs) that can be modified to follow
    [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md) and is related to the
    tuning task requested. **DO NOT** search without prompting first.
-   **Auto-Discovery: From Task to Huggingface:** If the user has a specific
    task (e.g. math reasoning, coding, instruction following) or wants to use a
    Hugging Face dataset without naming a specific one, refer to
    [Huggingface Datasets Reference](references/hf_datasets.md) and recommend
    matching datasets (e.g., `open-r1/OpenR1-Math-220k` or
    `AI-MO/NuminaMath-TIR` for mathematical reasoning; `openai/gsm8k` is also
    widely used). For each dataset recommended, provide some information about
    the dataset and provide some reasonable splits, and ask the user to select
    one. Do NOT output generic instructions telling the user to prepare and
    upload their own data — proactively guide the interactive dataset discovery,
    preview, and preparation flow.

    > [!IMPORTANT] **CRITICAL: Ask for Confirmation and Column Selection.** Once
    > the dataset is selected, execute Python via `run_command` to inspect the
    > dataset using `load_dataset(..., streaming=True)`. Do not proceed with
    > dataset preparation or upload until you perform the following steps and
    > get user confirmation: 1. **Dataset and Split Confirmation:** Present the
    > dataset and available splits to the user and have them confirm which to
    > use. 2. **Column Selection (Hugging Face or Custom Datasets):** You
    > must: - Provide a list of all available columns in the selected dataset
    > split. - **Show a few samples from the dataset** to help the user
    > understand the content and make the choice of columns. - Recommend which
    > columns should be mapped to `prompt` (or user message) and `completion`
    > (or assistant response), offering a few reasonable options if
    > applicable. - Ask the user to confirm the column mapping or specify which
    > columns to use.

    For distillation, map only the prompt column. The teacher model writes the
    responses, so no completion column is needed.

### 1.1 Formatting & Validation

-   **Conversion**: If data is in CSV, JSON, or Parquet, use
    `scripts/prepare_dataset.py` to convert.
-   **Validation Split Confirmation**: Except for prompt-only distillation data
    (next bullet), whenever generating or preparing a single dataset without an
    explicit validation set (including when generating sample chat/instruction
    datasets or preparing training datasets), you MUST generate or process the
    data using Python via `run_command` and **you MUST prompt the user** to seek
    permission to split the training dataset 90/10 to form a validation dataset
    (using `--validation_split 0.1` or Python script). If they agree, proceed
    with the split. If they decline, just use the training dataset without a
    validation dataset. Do **NOT** offer an 80/20 split; the tuning service
    rejects it, for the reason given in
    the
    [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md#sizing-the-validation-split).
 Do NOT proceed to upload the dataset or
    submit the tuning job before asking the user about the 90/10 validation
    split!
-   **Distillation training data**: Convert with `--prompt_only` and no
    `--completion_col`; see the
    [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md#distillation-datasets). Do
    **NOT** offer the 90/10 split for a prompt-only file: the split would have
    no responses, and a validation dataset must include them. Validation is
    optional for distillation; use one only if the user has separate data with
    responses, and convert it the normal way.
-   **Validation**: If data is already in JSONL, validate it before uploading.
    Simply having a `.jsonl` extension is not enough. You must verify that the
    content schema is valid for tuning (e.g. correct system/user/model roles).

```bash
python3 scripts/prepare_dataset.py \
    --input my_data.jsonl \
    --format <messages|messages_gemini> \
    --validate_only
```

*(Use `--format messages` for open models and `--format messages_gemini` for
Gemini models.)* - Refer to [Data Preparation Guide](references/data_prep.md)
for required schemas.

### 1.2 Upload

Upload formatted `.jsonl` files (both training and validation splits, if
applicable) to GCS using a unique directory (e.g., with a datetime timestamp) to
avoid overwriting outputs from different runs. If the user named a bucket (e.g.,
`gs://mybucket`), use that bucket name EXACTLY as provided (verbatim) and NEVER
prepend the project ID or modify the bucket name. Upload local `.jsonl` splits
to an existing bucket via `google.cloud.storage.Client` in Python (do NOT create
a missing bucket unprompted here; see Phase 3 if a bucket needs to be proposed
and confirmed):

```python
from google.cloud import storage

storage_client = storage.Client(project=PROJECT)
bucket = storage_client.bucket(BUCKET_NAME)
bucket.blob(f"tuning_agent_job_{TIMESTAMP}/train.jsonl").upload_from_filename(
    "/tmp/train.jsonl"
)
if VAL_DATASET_PATH:
    bucket.blob(f"tuning_agent_job_{TIMESTAMP}/val.jsonl").upload_from_filename(
        VAL_DATASET_PATH
    )
```

## Phase 2: Model Configuration & Recommendation {#phase-2}

Help the user choose the best model and parameters. **Always seek user
confirmation before submitting the job.**

-   If the user does not specify a specific model in their prompt, calculate
    recommendations based on the **Models Catalog**.
-   **Prompt for Confirmation:** Present the recommended model to the user and
    ask for their confirmation before configuring hyperparameters.

### 2.1 Configuration

#### For Open Models

-   Recommend `tuning_mode`, `epochs`, `learning_rate`, and `adapter_size` based
    on the [Tuning Guide](references/tuning_guide.md) and model-specific
    baselines in the [Models Catalog](references
